rationale: ACCEPT. All 16 executed controls pass (reference, empty, recomputed, answer-blind alternative, missing-file, and 10 probes), and I verified the public contract against the executable grader code rather than the author's prose. (1) Contract/implementation: the grader implements exactly the published rules - literal 9-name header in order, 9-field data rows, all-blank-or-all-present motif fields, coordinate domains (below 2^62, start<end, motif_start<motif_end), strand + or -, exact Decimal numeric equality for fc and motif_pval with NaN/Inf/whitespace rejected before any comparison, order-free Counter multisets with multiplicity, and structural gating (csv_format, value_domains, content) exactly as disclosed. No reference values, row counts, dimensions, hashes or control names are embedded; failure messages quote only submission-side values; the grader reads only the two CSVs, executes no submission code, touches no inputs, writes only the report, exits 0 with a complete five-check report in every executed case (missing/empty/malformed included), and fails all checks on a corrupt reference rather than passing. (2) Precision basis is defensible: fc and pval are pass-through decimal literals (5-decimal fc, integer pval in [384,1035] per the archived reference stats) with no arithmetic performed on them, so exact comparison is not a tolerance accommodating a wrong method; boundaries were executed - reversed order, trailing-zero stripping, exponent and quoted-field respellings all pass, while a last-digit fc perturbation, motif_pval +/-1, strand flips and NaN fail as designed. (3) Science: the graded artifact is the notebook's terminal export (hash-verified archive) projected 1:1 by header rename only (2484403 to 2484423 bytes, data rows unchanged; the archived column stats confirm the 9-field public schema covers it, including 5765 blank motif rows). Its conformance to the published rules - distinct-interval grain with first-record fc over the 15 duplicated intervals, max-pval with earliest-file-row tie-break over the 49 tie cases, +/-1 kb both-side expansion with base-sharing subtraction, assignment-before-trim decoupling, and blank motif fields for unannotated peaks - was established by an accounting-correct answer-blind independent implementation (different codebase and algorithm: bisect index versus heap sweep, executed without answer access, exit 0, all five checks passed against the reference despite different decimal spellings) plus an independent recomputation; the row arithmetic is internally consistent across all records (40587 records over 40572 distinct intervals, minus 15 fully removed = 40557 rows, 0 split peaks, 2 single-piece trimmed rows, 5766 no-motif peaks minus 1 fully removed = 5765 blank rows). (4) Wrong outputs fail meaningfully and with correct check isolation: the fabricated extra row, weaker/fabricated/substituted motif, exact row duplicate (set-vs-multiset), other-record fc on a duplicated interval, dropped blank-motif row and NaN each fail exactly the checks they should, per the executed reports verified field by field. Prose claims I could check held up against code and records, and portability/independence claims are properly scoped. Three candidate concerns were assessed and are non-issues for this artifact, with no repair warranted: (a) the materialization oracle's heap-sweep assignment has a latent over-inclusion pattern for hypothetical nested-peak inputs (motifs admitted by an earlier longer peak are not re-checked against the current peak's end, contradicting its comment), but it cannot manifest on the hash-pinned read-only inputs - the controlled construction-001 run produced output byte-identical to the projected reference, and the answer-blind implementation with correct per-peak overlap checks reproduced the same content - and the oracle is never executed by the grader, which grades against the projected reference; any future reuse should add a motif_start < gend re-check to that inner scan. (b) The grader enforces an undisclosed 64 MiB read cap (MAX_FILE_BYTES); unreachable by any compliant submission at this data scale (reference ~2.5 MB) and consistent with the task resource limits, though it would be prudent to disclose it in any future contract revision. (c) Prose-only nits: the addendum's claim that full_table_match is a direct function of the previous two content checks is not strictly true under duplicate (chrom,start,end) keys, and the implementation computes full-row multisets directly, which is the stricter and correct behavior; the independent solution's stale trimming counts (3 partially-trimmed / one split into two pieces) are contradicted by its own executed log (peaks split: 0, fully removed: 15), which is the direct measurement and matches the reference row arithmetic. None of these affects any executed control, the grading behavior, or any acceptance outcome, and modifying this candidate to address them would invalidate the hash-attached evidence chain for no scientific gain. The candidate is suitable for subsequent Harbor packaging with its own isolation/oracle checks.
